items.headline: August payrolls surge 162,000; unemployment stays 4.1%, reviving September Fed-hike risk
items.category: Macro / Labor / Federal Reserve / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, far above the 56,000 Reuters consensus. Unemployment held at 4.1%; average hourly earnings rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y. June and July payrolls were revised a combined 55,000 higher.
items.whyItMatters: The strong report reverses the weak-ADP narrative and reduces the case for an immediate dovish pivot. Market-implied odds of a September hike rose after the release. AGCI keeps duration staggered, hurdle rates elevated and avoids adding broad equity beta into extreme valuation.
items.agciSignal: LABOR RESILIENCE / SEPTEMBER HIKE RISK / HIGHER HURDLE RATE

items.headline: Greed jumps to 87 and regime returns to Mid Bull while Valuation remains 86
items.summary: The live AGCI engine reads Greed 87/100, up 10 points daily, Valuation 86/100, Mid Bull regime and EUPHORIA_RISK / Capital preservation — Do not chase.
items.whyItMatters: The prior correction signal has reversed before valuation normalized. AGCI treats the move as renewed complacency, not improved expected return, preserving 10–15% deployable liquidity and staged entries only inside fair value.

items.newsletter: Review & Preview — Manifesting Steady Rates / 3 Sep 2026
items.headline: Waller opens door to holding rates, but says neutral rate may be structurally higher
items.category: Federal Reserve / Fiscal / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Governor Christopher Waller said he would favor holding rates steady in September if August inflation confirms disinflation, but a renewed inflation setback could justify a hike. He separately argued that the historical Treasury safety premium has eroded, lifting the neutral rate amid fiscal borrowing and AI capital demand.
items.whyItMatters: The policy path is conditional, while the structural discount rate may be higher even without repeated Fed hikes. AGCI distinguishes a possible September hold from a return to low-rate valuation assumptions.
items.agciSignal: TACTICAL HOLD POSSIBLE / STRUCTURALLY HIGHER R-STAR / NO LOW-RATE RESET

items.headline: Hormuz traffic falls to four commodity vessels as oil posts steep weekly gain and diesel hits records
items.summary: Only four commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on Thursday, down from nine and far below the recent 10-day average near 15. Brent was around $94.77 early Friday and headed for a weekly gain above 6%; U.S. diesel prices reached record levels amid supply disruption.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock is now visible in physical flows and refined products, increasing inflation and transport-cost risk. AGCI keeps a moderate energy hedge but does not chase crude after the weekly surge.
items.agciSignal: PHYSICAL FLOW DISRUPTION / DIESEL INFLATION / MODERATE HEDGE

items.headline: U.S. 30-year mortgage rate rises to 6.71%, highest since July 2025
items.summary: Freddie Mac's average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 6.71%, a 13-month high, as Treasury yields and inflation-risk premia remained elevated.
items.whyItMatters: Housing affordability and transaction velocity face renewed pressure. AGCI retains +50/+100 bp real-estate stress, conservative DSCR and lower leverage rather than assuming cap-rate relief.
items.agciSignal: HOUSING FINANCING TIGHTER / KEEP +50/+100 BP STRESS

items.headline: Snowflake raises product-revenue outlook as AI drives roughly half of growth acceleration
items.summary: Snowflake raised fiscal-2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion from $5.84 billion after 37% quarterly product-revenue growth; management said AI accounted for approximately half of the recent acceleration.
items.whyItMatters: This is evidence that AI monetization is broadening from chips and servers into enterprise software consumption. AGCI still applies valuation discipline because Snowflake trades at a large premium to software peers.
items.agciSignal: AI SOFTWARE MONETIZATION CONFIRMED / PREMIUM VALUATION DISCIPLINE
